- harsh-ui-gates-not-taste
  - id: f383e7fa-2d67-4b4c-a350-8584710d378e
  - source: auto
  - usage_scenario: For interface design and visualisation work he wants hard, numeric, build-failing gates — measured WCAG numbers and token resolution, not subjective review
  - content: For UI and visualisation work, "устрой суровые проверки": build failing gates with published numbers
    as thresholds, not design opinions. Concretely what he accepted on 2026-10-26 in Raven:
    `tests/test_design_contracts.py` (token resolution across all three themes, WCAG 2.1 4.5:1 text /
    3:1 UI-part computed from the token hexes themselves, no hard-coded colour in chart props, every
    chart inside a `role="img"`-labelled card, no off-origin `src`/`href`, vendored fonts with a Cyrillic
    subset, `:focus-visible` present and no `outline: none` without a replacement, `viewBox` on inline
    SVG, landing anchors resolving), `web/src/design/accent.test.ts` (16 accent presets × 3 themes ×
    default/hover/active), plus the same idea for content claims (egress map, landing guards).

    **Why:** a design system that is only a naming convention, four `var(--dt-*)` lookups resolving to
    nothing, 2.54:1 grey text and eleven charts a screen reader announces as empty all "looked fine" in
    a screenshot at the author's monitor width. He asked for the checks after the sentence on the landing
    page turned out to be false, so he distrusts visual self-review.

    **How to apply:** measure first (compute contrast from the hexes, load the built page in the browser,
    `document.fonts.check`, `getComputedStyle`), then encode the measured number as the threshold; fix the
    palette/component rather than loosening the limit; when a limit is wrong for the role (an accent is a
    button surface, not text), state the role in the test with a comment instead of dropping the check.
    Never claim a visual property from spec or memory — check the browser, as with `var()` inside SVG
    presentation attributes, which turned out to work.

    The same pass in Wake (2026-10-26) showed which numeric checks actually pay, and each of these was a
    green gate hiding a real defect:
    - contrast must be computed against the **composited** background — every translucent ancestor layer
      plus translucent ink over them. "First opaque ancestor" let red status text sit at 4.44:1 on its own
      red chip underlay while the gate stayed green; and no alpha fixes a hue pair that fails (red-on-red
      needed a second token for text vs fill, not a looser threshold).
    - horizontal-overflow checks need two numbers: root `scrollWidth` and the `scrollX` the page reaches
      when asked to pan. A wide table inside a `position: static` `overflow-x: auto` container clips
      painting yet still inflates the document's scrollable area (measured: body 320, root 771, pan 451).
    - source-scranning style gates must match the forms the language actually writes: `outline: "none"`
      in a JSX object and the Tailwind `outline-none` both slipped past `/outline:\s*none/`, and `rgba()`
      literals escaped a hex-only palette check (12 sites in panels). A `var()` scan needs a balanced
      paren walk, not a regex stopping at the first `)` — nested `var(--a, var(--b))` and `rgba()` inside
      a fallback hid 16 sites until a self-check was written for the detector itself.
    - measure the **pre-hydration** frame, not just the settled page: when every theme token is injected
      by JS after mount, the built stylesheet alone paints `.card`/`.chip` as `rgba(0,0,0,0)` and only
      literal fallbacks — which can describe exactly one of several themes. Publish the tokens as a
      generated CSS sheet and gate it (regenerate in-test, compare, and assert the file is imported).
    - deleting a stale literal fallback is *worse* than leaving it if the declaration collapses: with the
      token unresolved, `background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--a), var(--b))` is invalid at
      computed-value time and a white-labelled button renders invisible. Order matters — publish the
      tokens first, then drop the literals, and verify by rendering the built CSS with no scripts.
    - a translucent brand colour is not a state indicator: `border-color: accent-muted` (alpha 0.15)
      composites to 1.13:1 over the card the control sits on, so hover and the 3px focus ring change
      invisibly while every static contrast gate stays green. Gate `:hover`/`:focus*` borders and rings at
      3:1 against the **panel** token, and clamp the runtime accent palette against the card, not the page.
    - canvases bypass the whole CSS layer (no `var()` resolution, so no theme awareness and no gate): read
      the palette from computed style per render pass, and clamp the categorical fills against the panel
      they are drawn on at the **text** threshold when the same token doubles as a badge label.
    - forbid third-party palettes too, not just hexes: framework utilities like `text-red-400`,
      `bg-green-900/30` are colours no theme owns, so they survive neither a theme switch nor an accent
      picker (19 sites in Raven). And prove the schema bites: delete one key per family and require a
      validation error, or `required` lists silently assert nothing.
    - derive every budget/volume fixture from a live measurement (row counts, timings) and mutation-test
      each new gate by reintroducing the defect: the tint test had to report exactly the 4.44 the browser
      had reported before it was trustworthy.
    - **a token family is scoped by the surface it was measured against, not by its hue.** Reusing
      `colors.chart.series-*` for tag badges looked reasonable and was wrong twice: the series gate
      asserts 3:1 against the **page**, while a badge sits on a **card**, so `series-1 #7c3aed` landed at
      2.74:1 — under the threshold the family's own gate claims; and it silently re-assigned what each
      colour means to the user (coding was blue, became green). Re-measure against the new surface, and if
      the values you would add are clones of existing keys, rename the family to role-neutral slots
      (blue/green/amber/… shared by every consumer) instead of adding duplicates.
    - **when a fix repaints something the user recognises, surface the decision with the numbers instead of
      shipping the repaint.** Flagged in one line at the end of a report ("esli hochesh drugoy nabor —
      skazhi") and he took it up the next message ("закончим с маппингом цветов") and had it committed as
      its own change. The accepted shape: state what the old colours were, what the new ones are, what each
      measures, and name the alternative — then implement whichever he picks rather than pre-empting him.
    - labels on saturated fills need the *picker* gated, not just the colour: `paint.ts labelOn()` chooses
      between the theme's two inverse colours, so the gate asserts that for every slot of the scale at
      least one of the two clears 4.5:1 — otherwise the runtime rule has nothing safe to choose.
    - **which threshold a pair is held to is itself a defect source, and it outlives the palette.** Every
      chart axis painted `text.tertiary` at 3.72:1 on the card and stayed green for weeks because the pair
      list asserted tertiary-on-card at the 3:1 *UI-part* threshold — tick labels are 9-11px, so they are
      normal text at 4.5:1. When a number passes, re-read which role the assertion claims, not only what
      the colour is; the same pass found a 10px-floor question resolved the same way (WCAG has no px floor,
      but the token scale starts at 12px, so anything smaller had walked past the scale).
    - **read the library, not your memory of it, before claiming what a surface paints.** Two claims I would
      have shipped wrong: recharts puts the axis `stroke` on the tick *text*
      (`CartesianAxis.js:61 stroke:'#666'`, `:352-353 fill: stroke`) — so retargeting the stroke really does
      move the labels, and an unstyled `<Tooltip>` is a `#fff` box with `#000` text
      (`DefaultTooltipContent.js:34,42`); and `@tailwindcss/typography` was **not installed** while five
      components carried `prose prose-invert` — the built bundle had exactly one `.prose` rule, and
      Tailwind's own preflight (`h1..h6{font-size:inherit}`, `ol,ul,menu{list-style:none}`,
      `a{color:inherit;text-decoration:inherit}`) was flattening the markdown the product renders. Grep the
      built CSS for the selector you believe styles your markup; "the class is in the JSX" proves nothing.
    - **a gate that matches zero things is the failure mode you will actually hit.** Mutation checks caught
      three vacuous gates in one session: `selector.endswith(" ul")` was satisfied by `.prose ul ul`, a
      substring test for `"underline"` was satisfied by `text-underline-offset`, and a JSX tag scanner whose
      `rf"<{name}\b"` lost its backslash to a quoted heredoc found **0 tags** and reported two green gates.
      So: index CSS by each selector in the comma list separately, compare whole declarations
      (`"text-decoration: underline" in body`), print the scanner's match count and treat zero as a broken
      probe, and run the mutation *before* believing the pass.
    - **before deleting a "dead" rule, check what it did, not only whether its class is used.** All 15
      per-theme utility remaps had zero class usages, and one of them (`[data-theme] .prose-invert`) was the
      only thing mapping prose colours to tokens — restored and re-declared as a plain `.prose` layer shared
      by all three themes (it had silently excluded the default dark theme). Also: undo your own mutation by
      writing back a string you saved, **never** `git checkout -- <file>` — that discarded 16 uncommitted
      retargets in the same file seconds after they were made.
    - offline surfaces (gateway-served webchat page, MV3 popup) cannot import the SPA sheet, so they embed a
      **generated** region between `design-tokens:start/end` sentinels and address it via `var()` with short
      local aliases. That is what exposed their private palettes: the chat page had invented
      `--accent #8b5cf6` and put `#fff` on it (4.23:1) while the app's own accent clears 5.70:1. Gate the
      region byte-for-byte against the generator, require every referenced token to be declared inside it,
      forbid any other colour literal in those files, and forbid an alias no rule reads.
    - **a layout gate must prove which font it measured.** In Wake the 320 px pass read a *system*
      fallback on both sides of CI: the e2e fixtures abort every non-owned origin, so the
      `fonts.googleapis.com` link never loaded, Segoe UI shaped the text on the author's machine and
      DejaVu Sans on the runner — one paragraph green locally, clipped by 3 px in CI. Fix = ship the
      fonts in the bundle (`@fontsource-variable`), wait for `document.fonts.ready` before measuring,
      and gate that every `.woff2` is first-party and each family actually loaded. Then a synthetic
      letter-spacing inflation stays useful as a *foreign-font* stress layer, calibrated against the
      widest measured fallback (`.14em` puts Inter where DejaVu was) and mutation-tested.
    - **a CSS block that is not scoped by theme is a theme bug waiting to be measured.** In the OneWatch
      storefront (2026-11-04) an unscoped "normalize old dark classes to white" block with `!important`
      silently beat the dark theme: 63 slate labels at 2.3:1, green accents on whitened panels at 1.8,
      white text on the light top bar at 1.0. Fix = scope the block to the light theme, add explicit dark
      pairs, then measure again — and gate the *absence* too, because he then ordered the toggle deleted
      (`ui.test.js` asserts no `id="theme-btn"`, no `toggleTheme(`, no `body.stealth-edition`, so a theme
      cannot creep back).
    - **contrast has to be computed against the composited stack in the browser, per view.** The shop gate
      walks catalog / product / cart / checkout / orders / contacts / footer, skips invisible and
      transparent-ink nodes, composites every translucent ancestor layer (`bg-white/[0.05]` over `#0B0F17`
      is fine, and an alpha-blind probe reported 14 false "white on white" failures) and requires the
      offender list to be empty at 4.5:1. Measured result went 47 offenders → 0. Thresholds to fix by
      repaint, not by loosening: Telegram blue with white ink was 2.6, "Добавлено ✓" 3.4, a green warranty
      note 2.3.
    - **accessibility gates need a different instrument per background kind, and each wrong pairing produced
      a false defect first** (both storefronts, 2026-11-10, 15 surfaces / 1063 text nodes finally at 0 fails):
      flat panels must be measured from **computed styles** (ink over the first opaque ancestor, alpha
      composed), never from screenshot crops — a sticky header crossing the line rect injected another
      element's pixels and invented six "1.63:1" violations on 9:1 text. Pixel sampling is only legitimate
      where glyphs actually overlap media: prove it by testing whether any `img/video/picture/canvas`
      intersects the line rect, not by "some ancestor has a background-image". And the glyph-ring estimate
      (average of pixels around each dark sample) systematically under-reads 11–13px Cyrillic because
      anti-aliased half-tones pull it toward the ink — 4.33:1 reported for text the style layer puts at
      5.99:1 — so keep it advisory and fail only on the dominant-background colours.
    - **keyboard/overlay probes have three own-failure modes that look like app bugs:** measuring
      `getBoundingClientRect()` immediately after `keyboard.press('Tab')` races the `:focus` style (a
      correctly revealed skip-link read as "focused at y=-65"); a control with `outline: none` is legal when
      the ring lives on the wrapper (`.field:focus-within`), so walk ancestors for it; and a dialog's open
      state must be read from `inert`/`aria-hidden`/state class, never from `aria-modal`, which stays
      present while closed. Prove `prefers-reduced-motion` by the **delta between two contexts** (40/87
      transitions with `no-preference` → 0 with `reduce`), because a single-mode probe sees "nothing
      animating" in both and reports a green that asserts nothing.
    - **WCAG 2.5.8 (24px) is the gate, 2.5.5 (44px) the advisory** — and the real offenders were the
      inconspicuous ones: a `tel:` link in the drawer footer (311×22) and breadcrumb links (51×20), fixed by
      `display:inline-flex; align-items:center; min-height:24px`, which costs no visible layout.
    - **a token/palette law is only as wide as the documents it is parametrized over.** tippy_on_base wave 20
      (2026-11-13): the design contract read the site stylesheet only while the app's other surface shipped its
      own inline palette, so the primary mobile screen was governed by nothing — the exact defects already fixed
      on the site (a translucent-tint label at 4.27:1, two raw `#fff` fills, a dead `--warning` token) had simply
      reappeared where no gate looked. Fix = drive every palette rule through one list of surfaces with a
      token-name map between them, and mutate **each surface's own file** to prove each new case bites.
    - **the gate's parser is part of the surface under test — make it assert its own coverage.** A `:root { … }`
      block whose last declaration ends at `}` rather than `;` was invisible to a regex that split on `;`, so one
      token per block went unmeasured in every theme while the gate stayed green. Fix = terminate declarations at
      `;`, `}` or end-of-string **and** assert that every name declared inside the parsed span is a name the
      parser returned. Same family: a span-containment test cannot see a one-line palette block — compare by
      overlap.
    - **a geometry/token assertion must be scoped to the elements that actually own that surface, not to
      every node matching the selector.** HAMONSHOP 2026-11-11: a release-visual button gate asserted
      `border-radius == 10px` on the whole `button, .cart-trigger, .menu-toggle, …` set and reported 139
      "radius 0px != 10px" anomalies — every one a false positive on *surface-less text controls* (header
      nav menu-group toggles, the `.story-bubble` layout wrapper whose visible circle is the inner
      `.story-ring` at 50%, `.cart-trigger`, the underlined `.cart-remove-btn`). The real `.btn-*`
      components were all correctly 10px. Fix = fire the check only when the element has a visible surface
      (non-transparent `backgroundColor` OR `borderTopWidth > 0` with a non-transparent `borderTopColor`),
      which keeps the gate able to fail on a genuinely broken button. **How to apply:** before touching
      production on a mass-anomaly signal, classify anomalies by whether the element carries the design
      component (grep the CSS for the class's own `border`/`background`/`border-radius`) and confirm with
      screenshots — a broad selector + a single token value is a test-assumption bug, not a UI bug
      ([[test-the-implementation-not-the-assumption]]).

    - **a mutation harness's "MISSED" is first a suspect mutation, not a suspect gate.** 2026-11-14
      HAMONSHOP: the parallax sign-flip planting replaced `--parallax-sign: .07` with `.045` — same sign,
      different magnitude — so both gates correctly stayed green and the harness reported two missed
      defects for one invalid planting. Before touching a gate, check that the planted text changes the
      *semantics the assertion claims* (flip the sign, don't resize it). Same wave: when two rules differ
      by one word (`.hero-copy` vs `.hero-sign`), plant by whole-line byte-exact text — a point replace on
      `translate` would hit both nodes and the "each element uses its own multiplier" assertion would
      prove nothing.
    - **measure geometry by rendered position, not by parsing computed style.** Chrome hands back
      `getComputedStyle(el).translate` with unresolved `calc(...)`, and `clip-path: inset()` collapses
      equal sides into a 3-value form that keeps spaces inside `calc()` — a naive `split(/\s+/)` cut the
      value apart and read a finished reveal as incomplete. What is stable: the document-space delta
      (`rect.top + window.scrollY`) between two scroll positions, and a paren-depth-aware side parser.
      Self-check the detector on one broken and one correct value, as with every parser above.

    See also [[evidence-not-delegation]],
    [[test-the-implementation-not-the-assumption]], [[cutting-edge-design-preference]].

- project-raven-local-work-loss-fear
  - id: bb7dd892-0f49-4c31-9e77-e6120aa6834d
  - source: auto
  - usage_scenario: Unpushed local work is the real risk in this repo — 2026-09-29 orphaned-commit scare, repeated push-credential windows, and the proof set to use when he asks «все залил с машины?»
  - content: On 2026-09-29 the user feared a large body of local work had been deleted. It had not: `git reflog` showed a `reset: moving to origin/main` that orphaned four commits (voice-input cleanup, DAG-scheduler consolidation, `runtime/tools.py` split, `gateway_runner` route extraction), and all of that content had re-landed on `main` via a later squash commit plus follow-ups. A full tree comparison found only three files present in the orphaned tip and absent from `main` — all three deliberately deleted afterwards.

    **Why:** This repo's release model has no git tags (removed on purpose in favour of a single `main` branch and an on-demand `:latest` Docker rebuild), and `main` sat two commits ahead of `origin/main`. So the only durable copy of recent work was the local `.git` directory, where unreachable commits survive just as long as the reflog does.

    **How to apply:** When he suspects lost work, prove it from reflog + `git fsck --lost-found` + file-tree comparison before saying anything reassuring, and state the numbers. Treat "unpushed" as the actual risk here — offer to push or to pin a rescue ref, and mention that `git gc --prune=now` would make orphaned commits unrecoverable. He declined to answer about a rescue branch once; re-offer rather than creating it silently.

    Status 2026-09-29: `main` is pushed and matches `origin/main`, so the single-copy window is closed for now — but it reopens with every local commit, and there is still no tag or release to fall back to. **The window reopened again on 2026-11-02 and push was once more unavailable.** After five more verified
    commits (`7b48ad6`, `8c84ac4`, `5b1ac8d`, `162c2b3`, `5441bf7` + follow-ups) `git push` failed with
    `Invalid username or token`, `gh auth status` reported the `GH_TOKEN` env token **and** the keyring token as
    invalid, and he authorized the push in words ("реализуй все и пуш как ВСЕ выполнишь") but had not yet sent a
    fresh token. Confirms the routine: run `gh auth status` **before** starting a multi-commit chain, tell him the
    token needs refreshing up front, and keep reporting the exact `origin/main..HEAD` count while work piles up
    locally. Never `git gc --prune=now` in that window. **Count as of 2026-11-02 evening: 10 commits
    `origin/main..HEAD`** (`6a4d715`, `7b48ad6`, `8c84ac4`, `5b1ac8d`, `162c2b3`, `5441bf7`, `8232b88`,
    `3df9406`, `e067f25`, `5a178e5`), tree clean, each one gated 12/12 locally, and he granted the push in words
    ("реализуй все и пуш как ВСЕ выполнишь четко и грамотно") without sending a token - so ask for it once per
    session and then keep going rather than stalling on the push.

    See [[project-raven-gap-assessment-2026-09-29]], [[feedback-push-once-with-inline-token]],
    [[feedback-verify-then-one-commit]].

    **2026-11-12 — «все залил с машины?».** Answered with the proof set, not reassurance: `git rev-parse HEAD
    origin/main` equal, `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` = 0, `git ls-files --others` = 0, and the only
    two dirty entries left were the `raven_old` gitlinks (see
    [[project-raven-debt-backlog-2026-11-10]] — measured there to contain nothing unique). Two habits this
    question keeps requiring: (1) a ` M` entry in `git status` on this box is often only a stale stat cache —
    compare `git hash-object <file>` against `git rev-parse HEAD:<file>` and say "identical, stat noise" rather
    than "uncommitted changes", then `git add` the file to clear it; (2) before claiming anything local is at
    risk, compare the local copy against the pushed tree by size/content and quote both numbers.

    **The window reopened on 2026-10-27 and push was not available at all.** Two verified design commits (`9f7988a`, `03a57b9`) sat local-only because GitHub rejected both stored credentials — the `GH_TOKEN` environment token *and* the keyring token — with `Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported for Git operations.`; `gh auth status` reported both as invalid. So the failure mode here is not only "forgot to push" but "cannot push": before planning a multi-commit chain, check `gh auth status` early and tell him the token needs refreshing rather than discovering it at ship time. He had deliberately withheld the push anyway ("Отложи push, закончим с маппингом цветов"), so the correct action was to keep the commits local, re-verify the gate, and report `origin/main..HEAD` = 2 explicitly. While the window is open, do not run `git gc --prune=now`, and treat any `reset`/`checkout` in this repo as needing a `git status` + `git log origin/main..HEAD` check first.

  - content: He asked what the ML part of Raven needs to reach "the peak of the project", then chose a concrete
    training path. Decisions recorded 2026-10-24:

    - **Training corpus: synthetic, generated from the live registry** — `ravencode.runtime.tools.
      get_tool_definitions()` (the same 66 definitions the MCP server reports and the landing page
      publishes). Split by `(language|tool, value bucket)`, not by random example.
    - **Base model: Qwen2.5-0.5B.** Chosen on a measurement, not reputation: on his Russian corpus text
      Qwen tokenizes at **3.04 chars/token vs 1.74 for SmolLM2** (same 4000 chars = 1314 vs 2299 tokens),
      and training is paid in tokens.
    - **Budget: 1000 pairs at p95 length × 3 epochs.** The corpus measured p50 119 / p95 159 / max 195
      tokens including the 51-token system prompt, so `max_length=192`; the shipped default of 512 would
      have spent **76.7 % of a night on padding**.

    **Hard limits, all measured on this box (see also [[reference-machine-profile]]):** CPU-only
    (`torch 2.14.1+cpu`, no CUDA), no `bitsandbytes`/`trl` → no QLoRA; ~60 tokens/s at 135M. So a real
    adapter is a 7-40 h overnight job, and "a model better than the hosted one we already call" is not
    reachable here. What *is* reachable and what I argued for: measured retrieval (ML-8), an eval loop that
    cannot lie (ML-3), A/B between models on persisted data (ML-7b), and only then a small adapter
    presented as a pipeline demonstration with a baseline pair.

    **`.venv-raven` has numpy and torch but NOT librosa or speechbrain** (measured 2026-11-02: PIL yes,
    librosa no, speechbrain no, torch yes). Consequence: every `speaker`-extra code path — the voice
    anti-spoof analysis above all — never executes in any local run or local test on this box, so a "green
    gate" says nothing about whether that control works; verify such branches by forcing the unavailable path
    in a test, or install `.[speaker]` first. Pillow **is** installed and declared in core dependencies, so a
    lazy `from PIL import …` is not evidence of a missing declaration.

    **Ad-hoc scripts must import the config layer before httpx (measured 2026-11-10).** This box exports
    `NO_PROXY=localhost,[::1]`, and httpx 0.28 turns `[::1]` into the URL pattern `all://[::1]` → every
    `httpx.get(...)` dies with `InvalidURL: Invalid port ':1]'` *before any request*. Raven sanitizes the
    variable at `raven.core.config` import time, so a throwaway probe script needs
    `import raven.core.config  # noqa` as its first import; without it the failure looks like a network or
    library bug. The same import is what makes `mkdocs`-less local checks possible: `mkdocs` is still absent
    from `.venv-raven`, so docs pages can only be validated locally by the YAML/nav guards, not by a build.

    **mypy DOES run on this box — never call a CI-only type error environmental (measured 2026-11-12).**
    `.venv-raven`'s mypy 2.4.1 wheel is mypyc-compiled: 232 `.pyd` files next to the `.py` sources, and
    Smart App Control refuses to load them, so `python -m mypy` died with `DLL load failed while importing
    mypy`. Force-reinstalling the official wheel does not help. The fix is to delete the `.pyd` copies inside
    `.venv-raven/Lib/site-packages/mypy` and `.../mypyc` — the wheel ships both forms, so the interpreter
    then loads the pure-Python modules (`mypy 2.4.1 (compiled: no)`) and the stage reproduces CI error-for-error:
    it caught `tests/core/auth/test_session_sweep.py:22 [no-any-return]`, the exact line all three CI jobs failed
    on, which had been written off as un-reproducible locally. Consequence: an unannotated fixture parameter
    returned from a `-> Path` fixture is a real gate failure (strict → `warn_return_any`), and a local green on
    types now means something. Cost: interpreted is several times slower than compiled, so watch the stage's
    `timeout=300` at `scripts/check_all.py:246`.

    **Toolchain parity with CI, measured 2026-11-11:** `.venv-raven` is Python 3.12.10 with mypy 2.4.1,
    ruff 0.17.4 and pytest 9.1.1 — the same versions CI installs. So a type or lint error that appears only in
    CI is *not* a version skew: it is either the editable-vs-installed difference (CI pip-installs
    `raven-agent`, this box has `-e`) or a warm cache. `--quick` is 8 stages and costs ~30 s here, but mypy
    answers in 1.7 s warm against 12 s cold, and the same flag can report 794 unannotated sites cold and 38
    warm — trust the cold number, and re-run cold before calling a local green a parity proof.

    See [[project-raven-gap-assessment-2026-09-29]], [[feedback-env-masking-in-ci-gates]],
    [[reference-github-actions-queue-stall]].

60-    - `c94911a` — 5 subprocess text reads pinned (`coding/git_integration._run`, `aios/api/bridge._rg_search`, `coding/test_generator`, `ravencode/cli/main` upgrade/pip, `scripts/check_all._run`) plus `tests/test_subprocess_encoding.py`. Measured failure modes, not guessed ones: ripgrep JSON *parses* fine but hands the caller `{'file': 'РєР»СЋС‡.txt'}`, and under an `ascii` locale the UnicodeDecodeError dies inside subprocess's reader thread so `stdout` comes back `None` → AttributeError → silent downgrade to the Python scan. `test_generator`/pip children also got `-X utf8` so their *own* output is UTF-8, not just our decode of it.
61-    - `4bb4bc6` — the same defect in file IO: 40 sites across `core/audit.py` (5 readers), `config_watcher`, `llm/providers/base`, `plugin_loader`, `secrets`, `tools_rbac`, `rag/embeddings`, `rag/vector_store`, `channels/webchat`, `cli/{deploy,init,service}`, `unique/plugin_marketplace` (8), `scripts/`; guard is `tests/test_file_encoding.py`.
62-    - **Security-relevant finding**: the signed audit chain reported `hash_mismatch` then `signature_mismatch` on its own untouched log whenever an entry carried non-ASCII — writers emitted UTF-8 bytes, readers decoded them as cp1251, so re-hashing a mojibake line could never reproduce the stored hash. Tamper detection produced a false alarm, which is how a real alarm gets ignored. His live `data/audit.log` measured clean: 9 entries, all `system.startup`, zero non-ASCII bytes — latent, never triggered.
63-    - Guard design worth reusing: a locale-dependent bug cannot be caught by a test on a UTF-8 runner, so `test_audit_chain_verifies_a_non_ascii_entry` re-executes the real `AuditLogger` in a child forced off UTF-8 mode (`-X utf8=0` + `PYTHONUTF8=0` + `PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0` + `LC_ALL=C`) and asserts `verify_chain`/`verify_signatures` stay valid. 3 of the file guard's 6 checks fail without the fix; both guards also self-prove by scanning a synthetic source that must report the exact expected lines.
64-    - AST scanner gotchas measured this session: `Path.open()` takes mode at `args[1]` but `X.open()` at `args[0]` after the receiver; `read_text`'s first positional IS the encoding while `write_text`'s first positional is content (so it never counts); arg-less `Path.open()` needs `and node.args` or the walker raises IndexError. Receiver allowlist (`Image`, `aiofiles`, `zipfile`, `socket`, …) keeps binary/foreign readers out of the report.
65-    - Adjacent suspicions closed with evidence instead of code: `plugin_worker` was already safe (binary `connect_read_pipe` + explicit UTF-8 decode, and it writes `json.dumps` ensure_ascii so its stdout is pure ASCII); `llm_providers/base` reads with the locale but its `_load_json` path is ASCII; and Starlette appends `; charset=utf-8` itself for `text/*` responses (verified for `text/plain` and `text/event-stream`), so Raven's responses were never at risk. `raven/core/_json.py` defaults to orjson → raw UTF-8, no `\uXXXX`, which is why the audit log's bytes were UTF-8 in the first place.

217-- feedback-target-processes-by-command-line
218-  - id: cb748f8b-5ebc-4e86-9784-dac0c427b69b
219-  - source: auto
220-  - usage_scenario: On this multi-session Windows box, never kill processes by image name — match the command line, because other agents' sessions run python/ssh here too
221-  - content: Stop a process only after matching its full command line (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "name='python.exe'" | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match 'doh_relay' }`), never by image name (`Get-Process ssh | Stop-Process -Force`, `taskkill /IM python.exe`).
222-
223-    **Why:** Several Qoder sessions share this machine — while working on tippy-on-base I saw Raven's `scripts/check_all.py` and its pytest workers running as `python.exe` in the same process list. Killing by image name silently destroys another session's work in progress, and `python.exe`/`ssh.exe` are the most shared names on the box. The same applies to anything listening on a shared port: a second `uvicorn :8000` or a stray tunnel client belongs to whoever started it, not to me.
224-
225-    **How to apply:** Before any process kill, list candidates with their command lines and pick the exact PID. If a service I did not start (Postgres, a dev server, a tunnel) is gone or a port is busy, investigate who owns it instead of restarting blindly — in one session the local uvicorn died mid-work without being touched by my commands. Related: [[feedback-repo-cleanliness]], [[reference-machine-cleanup-map]].

    def getfixturedefs(
        self, argname: str, node: nodes.Node
    ) -> Sequence[FixtureDef[Any]] | None:
        """Get FixtureDefs for a fixture name which are applicable
        to a given node.

        Returns None if there are no fixtures at all defined with the given
        name. (This is different from the case in which there are fixtures
        with the given name, but none applicable to the node. In this case,
        an empty result is returned).

        :param argname: Name of the fixture to search for.
        :param node: The requesting Node.
        """
        try:
            fixturedefs = self._arg2fixturedefs[argname]
        except KeyError:
            return None
        return tuple(self._matchfactories(fixturedefs, node))

    def _matchfactories(
        self, fixturedefs: Iterable[FixtureDef[Any]], node: nodes.Node
    ) -> Iterator[FixtureDef[Any]]:
        # Collect parent nodes and their IDs for matching
        parent_nodes = set(node.iter_parents())
        parentnodeids = {n.nodeid for n in parent_nodes}

        for fixturedef in fixturedefs:
            if fixturedef.node is not None:
                # Node-based matching: check if fixture's node is a parent
                if fixturedef.node in parent_nodes:
                    yield fixturedef
            elif fixturedef.baseid in parentnodeids:
                # Fallback to string-based matching for legacy/plugins
                yield fixturedef

=== authorize_request ===
from __future__ import annotations

import hmac

from fastapi import Request

from raven.core.auth.tokens import token_manager
from raven.core.config import get_settings


async def authorize_request(request: Request) -> bool:
    auth_header = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
    token = request.headers.get("X-Raven-Key", "")
    if auth_header.startswith("Bearer "):
        token = auth_header[7:]
    if not token:
        return False
    if await token_manager.validate_token(token):
        return True
    key = get_settings().web_secret_key.get_secret_value()
    return bool(key) and hmac.compare_digest(token, key)

=== sse_transport internals ===
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import Any

from loguru import logger


class SSETransport:
    def __init__(self, ping_timeout: float = 30.0) -> None:
        self._subscribers: dict[str, asyncio.Queue[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        self._running = False
        self._ping_timeout = ping_timeout

    async def start(self) -> None:
        self._running = True
        logger.debug("[sse] transport started")

    async def stop(self) -> None:
        self._running = False
        for q in self._subscribers.values():
            await q.put({"event": "close", "data": ""})
        self._subscribers.clear()
        logger.debug("[sse] transport stopped")

    def subscribe(self, client_id: str) -> asyncio.Queue[dict[str, Any]]:
        q: asyncio.Queue[dict[str, Any]] = asyncio.Queue()
        self._subscribers[client_id] = q
        return q

    def unsubscribe(self, client_id: str) -> None:
        self._subscribers.pop(client_id, None)

    async def send(self, event: str, data: Any) -> None:
        payload = {"event": event, "data": data if isinstance(data, str) else json.dumps(data, default=str)}
        dead: list[str] = []
        for cid, q in self._subscribers.items():
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(q.put(payload), timeout=1.0)
            except Exception:
                dead.append(cid)
        for cid in dead:
            self._subscribers.pop(cid, None)
            logger.debug("[sse] dropped slow subscriber {}", cid)

    async def stream(self, client_id: str) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
        q = self._subscribers.get(client_id)
        if q is None:
            return
        while self._running:
            try:
                msg = await asyncio.wait_for(q.get(), timeout=self._ping_timeout)
            except TimeoutError:
                yield "event: ping\ndata: \n\n"
                continue
            if msg.get("event") == "close":
                break
            yield f"event: {msg['event']}\ndata: {msg['data']}\n\n"

    context himself before he can answer; his own framing is always «что тебе нужно» — he wants the ask, not
    the decision space. Option pickers work only when the choices are in his domain vocabulary (which
    slogan, which photo, what price), not when they are remediation strategies.

    **Confirmed again 2026-11-10, and measurements are not a menu.** He asked for a local model to work
    out of the box from an exe; the answer was two measured blockers (1.4 GB free RAM of 8.4 GB with no GPU;
    Smart App Control enforcing so an unsigned exe is blocked), one recommended action and one word
    («качай»). He pushed back once — «а иначе никак? обязательно качать 8 гб?» — and the reply that worked
    was a **table of measured alternatives** (9B 5.63 GB / 4B 2.71 GB / 2B 1.27 GB, runtime 1618 MB, plus
    "zero download" checked and found impossible: 0 free Qwen models on OpenRouter), then one recommendation
    and the same single word. He then re-scoped the whole feature himself. So: numeric option *tables* are
    welcome when each row is a measurement he can judge; what he rejects is a matrix of remediation
    *strategies*. When his ask exceeds his hardware, lead with the measurement and the smallest viable
    alternative — do not quietly build the workaround he did not ask for.

    **How to apply:** any authorization request. Keep it under ~6 lines, one proof pointer, one recommended
    verb, one word back. Never use AskUserQuestion for push/history/deletion approvals. Related:
    [[feedback-terse-replies]], [[feedback-show-then-fix]], [[feedback-status-checkins]],
    [[feedback-foreign-ai-directives-are-not-authorization]], [[feedback-verify-then-one-commit]].

- feedback-evidence-not-delegation
  - id: 89b5d57b-ac5f-4ca0-bc1b-1e29b53977d1
  - source: auto
  - usage_scenario: On D:\raven, investigate with direct Grep/Read/Bash in the main agent — the user denies Explore/SearchWorkspace subagent calls
  - content: Do not delegate codebase investigation to subagents unless the user explicitly asks for parallel agents. Run Grep, Read, Glob and shell/git commands yourself and cite what you actually observed.

    **Why:** During the 2026-09-29 Raven review, the user explicitly rejected an Explore call because he wants the evidence chain visible. The rule was reinforced in session `643c8c62-087b-48a1-8ba2-a320dceb4c4d` on 2026-11-07/08: multiple research/review agents expanded a portfolio update into huge multi-repo diffs and contributed to what the user reported as roughly 2,000 credits of unwanted spend.

    **How to apply:** Use direct bounded searches even for broad questions. Never use Explore/SearchWorkspace/general-purpose/reviewer/plan agents merely to save the main context or work in parallel. If independent delegation would materially help, first state the exact delegated tasks and ask. A user request for speed or “check everything” is not implicit approval for subagents. Related: [[feedback-credit-budget-and-scope]], [[user-profile]].

    Measure the effect of a change before describing it, and publish the number even when it is smaller than the change you justified. 2026-10-24, tippy-on-base: collapsing `global_stats` from nine `SUM … WHERE kind = …` statements into one FILTER statement measured **130.5 → 115.6 ms** on a synthetic 300k-row journal — ~11%, not the 9× the framing implied, because reporting indexes already covered the per-kind sums. I said so in the commit and in the report, and moved the real justification to what the change actually fixes (nine statements were nine snapshots, and the ledger RLock does not span processes, so cross-process writers could make the landing counters sum a moment that never existed). He did not push back on the smaller number.

    **Why:** he reads the measurement, not the adjectives; an overstated win that he can disprove costs more trust than a modest one.

    **How to apply on perf work:** build the comparison so it is real (scratch DB + seeded rows + `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`, drop the DB afterwards), state both numbers, and when the win is thin, say what else the change buys — correctness, fewer round trips, one snapshot — instead of inflating the timing.

- feedback-verify-then-one-commit
  - id: 8491d450-080c-4762-b903-9d6b1ad64b50
  - source: auto
  - usage_scenario: Ship only with explicit scoped authorization after the full gate, local-only requests override prior push mandates
  - content: Commit and push only when explicitly authorized for the current scope; a green verification gate is not shipping permission. With an explicit "Проверяй всё и заливай всё что есть одним коммитом", verify first and ship the requested batch.

    **Why:** He was worried hours of local work had been wiped, so pushing *everything* in one move was the reassurance action. He also picked the full `check_all.py` run over the quick one when offered a menu, i.e. he prefers the slow, complete gate before anything is pushed. Confirmed the hard way in BotHive (Oct 2026): pushing test changes without running the gate locally cost five consecutive red CI runs before he said "ран красный братан" — each round was a 10+ min push/poll/fix cycle that one local `npm run coverage` would have caught in a minute.

    **How to apply:** Before pushing on his say-so: run the project's *full* gate locally first. Raven: `python scripts/check_all.py` (full, not `--quick`) plus `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint src && npm test -- --run`. BotHive (D:\EZOFFER, npm workspaces): `npm run check` (lint + build + typecheck) and `npm run coverage` — note `npm run build` skips `__tests__`, so only `typecheck` catches test-file errors. Then show `git status`/`git diff` for his review, make one commit, and push. Do not squash or force-push already-published commits to "make it one commit" — add a new commit instead. Push authorization is per-occasion: ask again next time.

    When several commits have piled up **unpushed**, "одним коммитом" is literal: squash them before the push. Tippy 2026-10-19 — "лей все на гитхаб 1 коммитом и пушем чтобы локально по проекту ничего не осталось на машине" — was satisfied by `git reset --soft origin/main` + one commit + a normal fast-forward push of 5 local-only commits (no force, nothing published was rewritten), with the composed message listing each squashed part. Same phrase also means the end state must be verifiably empty: clean `git status` plus `origin/main...HEAD` = `0 0`, reported back to him. Gitignored leftovers (`.env`, `.pytest_tmp/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `.wrangler/`) are not "leftover work" — name them, keep `.env`, and ask before deleting anything that looks regenerable.

    The authorization covers the commit and push only. Anything downstream that touches shared state stays his call even when it is the obvious way to finish the job: release workflows that publish container images, tags or GitHub Releases, and deleting files that merely look duplicated. Commit and push, then name the remaining step and hand him the command. **Never substitute a per-file check for the gate's own target list.** Raven 2026-10-24: I shipped
    three commits after running `ruff`/`mypy` on just the files I had edited, and all three red-lit
    `Check (Windows)` *and* both `Check & Test` matrices — mypy over the gate's full list
    (`raven/ aios/ ravencode/ plugins/ tests/ scripts/*.py`) reported 10 errors, every one of them in my
    own **new test files** (`Module "x" does not explicitly export attribute "time"` from patching
    `module.time`; six unused `type: ignore`; a lambda whose value was `list.append`'s None). Per-file
    runs miss those because `tests/` behaves differently as a package root, and unused-ignore detection
    needs the whole graph. The tests themselves were fine — CI ran 6496 + 2700 + 6457 green under the same
    commits — so the damage was purely mine and purely avoidable with `check_all.py --quick`, which takes
    under a minute once the mypy cache is warm. Same lesson in the other direction: a fix that changes a
    `-> list[...]` return is a contract change, and running the real gate found it (`test_manage_below_
    warning_returns_unchanged` asserts identity, `is`, not equality). **The lesson repeated two days
    later, same shape:** I edited a test file alongside the source, ran `ruff`/`mypy` over the four source
    files plus the *other* test files, and reported the cluster as verified — the staged gate's `--quick`
    then failed on `Item "None" of "Any | None" has no attribute "recorded"` in the one test file I had
    touched and not typechecked. Two rules follow, and they are the reason to run the gate rather than
    simulate it: (1) the check set is defined by the gate's target list, never by "the files I opened";
    (2) `--component <x>` runs in Raven **skip ruff and mypy entirely**, so a chain of component batches
    carries no type verdict at all and must be paired with `--quick`.

    **An accumulated tree of already-verified waves ships as ONE commit when the clusters interleave inside the
    same files.** 2026-11-14, Raven: ten waves sat in one working tree (94 paths), several of them editing the
    same modules (`config.py`, `middleware.py`, `admin_api.py`) and all of them documented in the single
    `CHANGELOG.md` file, so a per-wave commit needed hunk-level staging across one shared bullet list — the
    wrong-split risk cost more than the coarse commit. Executed shape he was told about plainly: one green
    16-check gate over the final tree, one commit whose body enumerates each wave with its measured number, and
    one CHANGELOG bullet per wave so the record stays wave-level even though the commit is cluster-level. This
    does not soften the 2026-11-02 rule above: an *unverified* batch still gets a commit per verified feature —
    the one-commit exception is for work that is already finished, documented and covered by the same gate run.

    See [[project-raven-container-verification]], [[project-raven-local-work-loss-fear]].

    When he pre-withholds it — e.g. 2026-10-12 "коммитов и пушей не делай без разрешения моего" before a full-repo audit, or 2026-10-15 "ты делай, но не коммить ничего" — the whole task runs with changes sitting uncommitted even after a green full gate; report the diff and wait. The release is also staged: "сделай все что нужно и коммить локально" (2026-10-15) authorized a local commit while push stayed a separate explicit command. An open-ended "продолжай дальше работать и улучшать" in reply to a commit request is consent to keep working, never consent to ship; ask for the commit explicitly every time. "чини все что в твоих силах ща" (2026-10-15) validated the terminal pattern for a withheld push: fix everything in scope, run the full gate, make ONE local commit, then close with an explicit list of what stays on his side (redeploy, push word) — he accepted that ending without pushback.

    **Commit and push are two separate grants, and he splits them deliberately.** 2026-10-27, same session: "Создай коммит без push", then "Отложи push, закончим с маппингом цветов" — the push was held not because verification failed (the full staged gate was green) but because he wanted one more design decision settled first. So: commit when told, keep going, and do not treat a green gate as a licence to push. When he then repeats "создай коммит" for work you already committed, **verify and confirm rather than commit again** — `git log --oneline -3`, `git status --short` (clean), `git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline`, and report the existing hash; an empty or duplicate commit is noise he would have to undo.

    A second commit that corrects a decision inside an *unpushed* first one is the accepted shape (2026-10-27: `9f7988a` improvised a colour mapping, `03a57b9` replaced it) — fix forward with its own measured commit message instead of amending, and state in the commit which verifications were re-run versus carried over from the earlier green run.

    **A granted push token can also be a rolling mandate for the session.** 2026-10-28: "дальше все делай
    расширяй и улучшай и заливай" plus "токен нигде не пали … чисто на разовый пуш" — after that each
    verified increment was committed *and* pushed without re-asking (six commits, one full staged gate per
    increment), the token used only inline in the push/fetch URL, nothing persisted, and the revoke
    reminder repeated at the end. Two limits held anyway: the standing mandate did not cover anything
    downstream of the push (release workflows, tags, GHCR) and it expired the moment he next said
    "отложи push" mid-task — treat such a phrase as revoking the standing grant for the work in flight,
    keep going locally, and ask again before the next ship.

    **"Заливай все обновления" / "займись всем что нужно" is that same rolling mandate.** 2026-11-01
    (Watchop): eight commits went out in one session, one per verified feature batch (multi-admin → admins
    roster → discounts → search fix → bulk import → full admin → publish), each preceded by the project's
    full gate (`npm test`, `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`, mirror-parity check) and followed by
    `gh run watch --exit-status` plus a Pages build check before I moved on. He never re-asked and never
    objected to the volume — the unit of work he expects shipped is the *feature*, not the whole session.
    Answering his "что надо сделать?" with a short numbered list of what is left and which items only he
    can supply (real photos, a MAX token) was accepted without pushback.

    **"Реализуй все и пуш как ВСЕ выполнишь четко и грамотно" (2026-11-02, Raven) is the same rolling
    mandate with an explicit quality condition.** He authorized implementing the whole identified backlog
    *and* pushing it once everything was verified — so push without re-asking per batch, but only after the
    project's full gate is green for that tree, and commit each verified batch separately rather than one
    giant commit. One practical consequence he accepted without comment: if I edit files that gate stages
    read *while* a gate run is in flight, that verdict no longer describes the tree, so the honest move is to
    stop the run (by command line, never by image name —
    [[feedback-target-processes-by-command-line]]) and re-run once the edits are complete, instead of
    committing against a stale PASS.

    **Do not request a token when the machine already has working creds.** Same session: `gh auth status`
    said the GH_TOKEN was invalid and the keyring timed out, yet `git push origin main` worked through
    Windows Credential Manager. Probe the transport (`git ls-remote origin`) before asking — he expects the
    push to just go once the gate is green. An app's own publish credential (a `GITHUB_PUSH_TOKEN` the bot
    reads from `.env` because he asked for publishing from the bot) is product configuration, not a licence
    to persist a token he pasted into chat; [[feedback-push-once-with-inline-token]] still governs those.

    **2026-11-07 clarification:** "все исправляй и делай интерфейс и дизайн пиковыми" did not authorize shipping. During the same shop task the user explicitly said "сейчас ничего не пуш, делаем локально"; all work and verification stayed local. In website discussions, "залить фотографии" can mean placing assets in the local interface, not Git push or deployment. That local-only ban was lifted in the same repo on **2026-11-10** by "запуш все что мы сделать" and, when the push had already gone, "все заливай на гитхаб, всю нашу работу я боюсь уже" — i.e. an accumulated multi-day batch may ship in one commit once verified, and re-asking per path is not expected.

    **After any `pull --rebase`/merge, prove the resulting tree still contains the whole intended payload before you call the push done.** HAMONSHOP 2026-11-10: a commit + `pull --rebase origin main` + push landed 363 files but silently dropped exactly one — the rebase took origin's blob for the conflicted `index.html`, erasing the entire static-demo redesign, while the e2e gates asserting that redesign shipped in the same commit (so `origin/main` was red on its own tests). Detection that worked and costs seconds: compare the changed-file *name sets* of `git diff --name-only <base> <local-commit>` vs `<base> <new-head>` (`comm -23`), then `git diff <new-head> <local-commit> -- <file>` to see what was eaten; recover with `git checkout <local-commit> -- <file>` and re-apply the other side's hunks by hand. **Why:** a rebase can "resolve" a conflict by discarding one side, and git will report a clean tree and a successful push while doing it. **How to apply:** never treat a fast-forward-looking push as proof of completeness — diff the pre-rebase commit against the pushed one, and report the file-count parity number.

    **"Все актуальное запушь с машины" (2026-11-11, tippy) is a request to enumerate, not just to `git push`.** The
    branch was already in sync, so the only real content was an untracked operational script. What he accepted:
    `git status --untracked-files=all` + `git branch -vv` + `git stash list` + `git log origin/main..HEAD` to prove
    nothing else was unshipped, then judge the one candidate on public-repo terms — read it end to end for
    credentials, confirm the heavy/derived artifacts beside it are gitignored, delete a dead machine-local path it
    still named (proved dead from the live process command line, per [[feedback-prove-dead-before-deleting]]),
    re-run the affected gates plus the script's own read-only probe, commit, push, and close with byte-identity of
    the pushed blob and `main == origin/main, working tree clean`. State what stayed out and why instead of silently
    leaving it untracked. Scope: he said "с машины" inside one project — do not read it as a fleet-wide mandate to
    push other repos.

    **Why:** The user deliberately separates implementation/content review from publication; third-party chat screenshots can contain looser wording while their own direct restriction remains in force.

    **How to apply:** Treat the newest explicit local-only instruction as overriding any earlier rolling shipping grant. Continue editing and testing, but require a new explicit commit/push/publication instruction; do not infer it from "fix all", preview approval or pasted photo correspondence.

- feedback-test-the-implementation-not-the-assumption
  - id: 8ab86384-c681-4078-9642-5e24982adab5
  - source: auto
  - usage_scenario: Mock-based integration tests must be derived from the real source under test, and a failing test is fixed in the test unless the implementation is genuinely wrong
  - content: Before writing or fixing a test, read the implementation it exercises and copy the contract from it exactly: symbol names, action/method names, argument shape (positional vs object), payload keys, required-vs-optional fields, every exported name the code imports, and the literal error strings.

    **Why:** In BotHive, five red CI rounds came from integration tests written against assumed SDK/worker behaviour — wrong action name (`say` vs `sendMessage`), wrong payload keys (`channelId/messageId/emoji` vs `channel/timestamp/name`), object assertions for positional SDK calls (`like(uri, cid)`), a missing mock export (`LogLevel`), a missing mock method (`app.event`, `rt.detectFacets`), and a regex that didn't match the platform-prefixed message (`Unknown Slack action: x`). None were bugs in the workers.

    **How to apply:** When a test fails, first determine which side is wrong by reading the source, not by editing the assertion until it passes. Keep production behaviour authoritative and change the test to match it; only touch the implementation when it is actually broken. Watch for tests that assert a *valid* input is rejected — check the real guard condition (`!token || !botId` means you must omit a field to trigger it). Fixtures written straight into a store must use the shape the code under test actually serializes, not the shape of the API response that fed it — in Wake a `Session` is camelCase (`userId`/`expiresAt`) while the sign-in response is snake_case, and hand-writing the latter into `localStorage` made the "expired session" test pass through the malformed-record branch instead of the expiry branch. A case labelled "missing token" must be missing only the token. The same discipline applies to a
    suspected defect before it becomes a change request: in Raven 2026-10-22 an "unclosed file handle in
    `PdfReader(str(path))`" was disproved by reading the wheel (`_initialize_stream` does
    `with open(...) as fh: BytesIO(fh.read())`, so the OS handle is already closed and `close()` only drops
    the in-memory buffer) — the refactor was reverted instead of shipped under a false commit claim.

    **Sharpest sub-case: a test that proves "degrades gracefully when the optional dependency is
    missing" by *assuming* it is missing.** In Raven this appeared twice in one week. Both times the fix
    was to patch the availability flag (`_TORCH_AVAILABLE`, `_CLIP_AVAILABLE`) instead of hoping the
    import fails, and both times installing the declared extra exposed a *real* production bug hiding
    behind the fake: the CLIP variant had been masking `ValueError: Sequence length must be less than
    max_position_embeddings` — `MultiModalRAG._embed_text_clip` never truncated, so indexing any chunk
    over ~77 tokens crashed on every machine that had transformers installed.

    **Why it also costs time:** 34 test constructions each loaded `openai/clip-vit-base-patch32` because
    `MultiModalRAG.__init__` reaches for it whenever transformers is importable — 1.7 GB pulled into the
    HF cache and minutes added to every unit batch, invisible in CI where the extra is absent.

    **How to apply:** when adding or bumping an optional extra, grep the suite for tests that branch on an
    availability flag *without setting it*, and for constructors that load a model at import/init time.
    Unit tests must never download weights; force the absent state in an autouse fixture and give the
    present path its own fake-backed tests. See [[feedback-evidence-not-delegation]],
    [[project-raven-local-env]].

    **Verification scripts have assumptions too — recompute the metric before reporting anything as missing.** HAMONSHOP 2026-11-10: a 25-item "is the work on GitHub" audit printed 2 FAILs that were purely my own metric bugs — `new Set(rows.map(r => r.code)).size` counted `undefined` as a 208th price-list code (real answer: 207 codes + 3 codeless leg rows), and `match(/^test\(/gm)` counted 25 specs while I had claimed 26 (the extra `test(` hits were regex calls, and the run itself was 25 specs × 3 projects = 75). I had already told him "26 спеков" from the log's numbering, and the false FAILs made shipped work look broken. **How to apply:** derive every expected constant from the data's actual shape (filter nulls before deduping; read the runner's own summary line for test counts), and treat a FAIL in a home-grown audit as a hypothesis about my script until it reproduces against the source of truth — especially when the FAIL would mean the user's work is missing.

    **Browser probes carry the same assumption problem — re-measure before reporting.** WATIX storefront
    2026-11-11: four "findings" died when the probe was fixed, and each would have become a fake change request:
    - badge digits reported `dx −5.9 / dy −3` because the probe appended its own absolutely-positioned `<span>`
      inside a flex badge and measured that. Measuring the digit's real layout box with a `Range` over
      `selectNodeContents` gave `dx 0 / dy 0` — no bug existed.
    - a "stuck responsive element" scan reported 8 dead nodes at 390 px because it only checked *whether* a
      `sm:`/`md:` display variant existed, not whether the viewport had reached that breakpoint. Below the
      breakpoint `display:none` is correct.
    - `loading="lazy"` images below the fold report `naturalWidth === 0` at first paint (8/10 loaded at 390 px);
      after a scroll they were 10/10. Absent ≠ broken.
    - a "file missing from the repo" verdict came from the probe's own path candidates (`SRC/public/<rel>`
      instead of `SRC/public/uploads/<rel>`); `git archive <sha> | tar -x` of the real tree showed both files
      present and the server answering 200.

    **How to apply:** when a scratch probe reports a defect, first ask what the probe itself did to the DOM,
    what breakpoint it compared against, and which paths it tried — then re-measure with the browser's own
    layout APIs (`Range`, `getBoundingClientRect` on the real node) before telling him. The genuine bugs in that
    same wave were only found by sweeping the *source of truth*: `.hidden{display:none !important}` in the
    insurance `<style>` layer silently suppressed every `hidden sm:inline` / `hidden md:block` (9 nodes never
    rendered: desktop search, top-nav item, both header labels), and the newly revealed `|` separator measured
    1.4:1 contrast. Encode each closed finding as a permanent build-failing gate rather than a one-off number.
    See [[harsh-ui-gates-not-taste]], [[feedback-exhaustive-sweep-and-drift-gates]],
    [[feedback-reaudit-remembered-findings]].

    **Browser-gate flakiness has implementation-side root causes too (HAMONSHOP 2026-11-08/09).** On a cold
    Next dev server, `locator.fill()` before hydration is silently reset by React's controlled inputs —
    wait for `networkidle` and re-verify `inputValue()` stuck (retry loop). Masked tel inputs reformat
    `+79991234567` to `+7 (999) …`, so equality checks must compare digits, not strings. Reading
    `getComputedStyle(...).transform` immediately after `mouse.down()` races a .12 s transition — use
    `expect.poll` while the button is held. And a gate that fails only in the full suite but passes alone
    on this shared 8 GB box is usually load from another session's server, not a regression: re-run in
    isolation, then once full, before touching production ([[reference-machine-profile]]).

    **Two more assumption bugs from HAMONSHOP 2026-11-12, both nearly filed as real defects.**- A catalogue image-integrity sweep reported **134 missing webp files**. The probe ran `fs.existsSync(p.image)`
      with cwd = the Next project root, while `catalog.json` stores public-relative paths (`img/nf-00000185.webp`)
      that live under `public/`. Re-run against `public/<path>`: 210 entries, 134 referenced, **0** missing. A
      "everything is broken" count in a home-grown sweep is a probe-path bug until the correct root disproves it —
      same class as the `SRC/public/uploads` miss above.
    - A third-party signing test that recomputes the signature with the **same helper the production code uses**
      proves only self-consistency and can never fail on a contract mismatch (the Tinkoff Token test re-derived
      SHA-256 over all sorted scalar values, exactly as `lib/tbank.ts` does). For any external API where the peer
      computes the same value independently, the assertion has to come from the vendor's documented field list or
      from a recorded real response — otherwise say plainly "contract unverified" instead of "test green".
    See [[feedback-security-gates-must-fail]], [[harsh-ui-gates-not-taste]].

    **WATIX audit 2026-11-12: four more self-inflicted "findings" retracted in the closing report.** The
    instrument bugs were (a) `fetch()` — in Node *and* in-page — transparently decompresses, so its byte
    count was reported as "wire size" and overstated the storefront 4.5× (183 КБ claimed vs 40.4 КБ br
    actually transferred); (b) a `page.evaluate` callback cannot see Node-scope variables — my parameterised
    id came back `id is not defined`, and `p.evaluate((pid)=>{…}, id)` is the fix; (c) a DOM selector looking
    for the stock banner also matched the related-products cards, which invented a PDP contradiction that did
    not exist once the probe was scoped to the banner itself; (d) a 404 for `/manifest.webmanifest` was my
    guessed filename — `manifest.json` is linked and serves 200. **How to apply:** before reporting any
    number from a scratch probe, name the instrument that produced it (decoded vs transfer bytes, which node
    the selector actually matched, which path it requested) and re-measure. When a wave does surface real
    defects, lead the reply with the retractions of my own earlier numbers — he re-plans on them.
    Harness and recipes: [[reference-watchop-audit-harness]].

    **UI gates must read identifiers from the rendered node and wait on state, never on a pause (Wake
    2026-11-13).** Two fail-opens lived in the e2e suite for a long time:
    - `visitTab` clicked a tab and then slept a fixed 900 ms. React keeps the already-mounted panel while a
      lazy one suspends (Suspense fallback only renders on first mount), so after the sleep the DOM still
      held the *previous* section — the probe measured the wrong panel and passed. Deleting the sleep broke
      five gates at once; asserting "a `[role=tabpanel]` exists and has no `.skeleton`" broke the same five,
      because the stale previous panel satisfies that too. What is both durable and fast: assert
      `aria-selected="true"` on the clicked element, then take that node's rendered `id` and wait for
      `[role="tabpanel"][aria-labelledby="<id>"]`, then require zero `.skeleton`. Suite went 5.4–7.5 min with

## HTTP transport (advanced)

The gateway also exposes the same protocol over HTTP when `raven start` is running:

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `POST /mcp/rpc` | Any JSON-RPC MCP call (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) |
| `GET /mcp/tools` | Tool list in plain JSON |
| `POST /mcp/tools/{name}` | Direct tool call with `{"arguments": {...}}` |
| `GET /mcp/health` | Liveness probe |
| `GET /mcp/events` | Server-sent events stream |

HTTP access requires a token: pass your `web_secret_key` as `X-Raven-Key: <key>` or
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A minimal remote-client config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "raven": {
      "url": "http://your-server:18888/mcp/rpc",
      "headers": {"X-Raven-Key": "your-key"}
    }
  }
}

So a stale `fd.node` identity permanently hides the fixture.

Why is `fd.node` a *different* Package instance? Because there are TWO `Package` nodes in the chain: 'tests' and 'tests/core' — and `fd.node` is `<Package core>`... it should be the same object as the chain's Package core.

With 3 args including a root-level file in between, pytest may re-create Package nodes (the `tests` Package gets created when collecting `tests/test_onboard.py` — since `tests/__init__.py` exists, `tests/test_onboard.py` is inside Package 'tests'). So collecting onboard may have triggered creation of the `tests` Package node, which didn't exist before (because args so far were files under tests/core, so pytest built Dir '.' → Package 'tests'? no...).

pytest's `Session.perform_collect` → for each arg, `genitems` uses `self.getnodeattr`/`collect` path resolution via `_collectfile`/`_join_parts`, which memoizes nodes in `self._nodes_by_path`. In the failing order, the memo for `tests/core` may be populated by a Package node created during the onboard arg... 

I don't need to fully explain pytest's internal churn. The actionable root cause is precise and citable: **`_pytest/fixtures.py:_matchfactories` yields a conftest fixture only when the exact `Package` node object captured at parse time is in the item's parent chain; it never falls back to the `baseid` string once `fixturedef.node` is set. When the same directory is collected through two different arg paths in one session, pytest can build a second `Package` instance for `tests/core`, the identity check fails, and every fixture from `tests/core/conftest.py` disappears.**

Is that a pytest bug worth reporting upstream? It looks like one (the `elif` should be `or`). Worth mentioning, and there's a legitimate workaround in the repo.

**The fix in our repo** (durable, no pytest patching): don't rely on directory-conftest fixture *visibility*; import the fixtures explicitly into the modules that use them. Two options:
(a) Move `switch_env`/`switch_names` into `tests/conftest.py` (root, whose nodes are stable?) — the same bug could hit `tests` Package too (its baseid 'tests' is in the chain; fd.node would be `<Package tests>` — could also go stale). Risky.
(b) Define the fixtures in a plain module, e.g. `tests/core/switch_fixtures.py`, and `from tests.core.switch_fixtures import switch_env, switch_names` in each test module that needs them → registration happens against the *module* node of the importing test file, which is always in the chain. Robust and explicit.
(c) Put them in a pytest plugin registered via `-p` in pyproject `addopts`.

(b) is the cleanest: minimal, local, and immune to Package-instance churn. Also fixes the ordering fragility permanently.

Which files use them? `tests/core/test_runtime_switches.py` and `tests/core/test_config_watcher.py` (grep switch_env/switch_names usage).

Note: importing a fixture function into a module — pytest picks up imported fixture names if they're module attributes (yes, that's how pytest plugins/fixtures work: `parsefactories` scans module `__dict__` for `_pytestfixturefunction` markers). Need `# noqa: F401` for ruff.

        assert unguarded == [], f"request a switch fixture without importing both: {unguarded}"

`ravencode/runtime/workspace.py:confine` against the root the process resolves — the `--workspace`
the server was given, else the deployment's root — and the policy that gates the call resolves the
same directory, so it never refuses a path the tool would have accepted. The tool is the stricter of
the two: it does not open the system temp directory. A path outside the root raises
`PermissionError` inside the tool.

A refused call answers `[denied] ...` with `isError: true` over JSON-RPC and HTTP 403 on
`POST /mcp/tools/{name}`. The one thing MCP does not inherit is `TOOLS_PROFILE`: the named
profiles list plugin tool names (`files.read`, `api.http_get`), this registry serves `read`
and `http_get`, and an allow-list of names that can never match reads as a blanket refuse.
 The orchestrator builds the same policy with `profile="full"` for the same reason.

## HTTP transport (advanced)

The gateway also exposes the same protocol over HTTP when `raven start` is running:

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `POST /mcp/rpc` | Any JSON-RPC MCP call (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) |
| `GET /mcp/tools` | Tool list in plain JSON |
| `POST /mcp/tools/{name}` | Direct tool call with `{"arguments": {...}}` |
| `GET /mcp/health` | Liveness probe |
| `GET /mcp/events` | Server-sent events stream |

HTTP access requires a token: pass your `web_secret_key` as `X-Raven-Key: <key>` or
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A minimal remote-client config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "raven": {
      "url": "http://your-server:18888/mcp/rpc",
      "headers": {"X-Raven-Key": "your-key"}
    }
  }
}
```

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import Any

from loguru import logger

# A subscriber that cannot keep up is dropped rather than allowed to grow without bound: an
# unbounded queue made the drop path below unreachable, and one wedged client stalled every
# publish for its whole timeout.
_MAX_PENDING = 256


class SSETransport:
    def __init__(self, ping_timeout: float = 30.0, max_pending: int = _MAX_PENDING) -> None:
        self._subscribers: dict[str, asyncio.Queue[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        self._running = False
        self._ping_timeout = ping_timeout
        self._max_pending = max_pending
        self.dropped = 0

    async def start(self) -> None:
        self._running = True
        logger.debug("[sse] transport started")

    async def stop(self) -> None:
        self._running = False
        for q in self._subscribers.values():
            q.put_nowait({"event": "close", "data": ""})
        self._subscribers.clear()
        logger.debug("[sse] transport stopped")

    def subscribe(self, client_id: str) -> asyncio.Queue[dict[str, Any]]:
        q: asyncio.Queue[dict[str, Any]] = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=self._max_pending)
        self._subscribers[client_id] = q
        return q

    def unsubscribe(self, client_id: str) -> None:
        self._subscribers.pop(client_id, None)

    async def send(self, event: str, data: Any) -> None:
        if not self._running:
            return
        payload = {"event": event, "data": data if isinstance(data, str) else json.dumps(data, default=str)}
        for cid in list(self._subscribers):
            q = self._subscribers[cid]
            try:
                q.put_nowait(payload)
            except asyncio.QueueFull:
                self._subscribers.pop(cid, None)
                self.dropped += 1
                logger.warning("[sse] dropped subscriber {} after {} undelivered events", cid, self._max_pending)

    async def stream(self, client_id: str) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
        while True:
            q = self._subscribers.get(client_id)
            if q is None:
                return
            try:
                msg = await asyncio.wait_for(q.get(), timeout=self._ping_timeout)
            except TimeoutError:
                yield "event: ping\ndata: \n\n"
                continue
            if msg.get("event") == "close":
                return
            yield f"event: {msg['event']}\ndata: {msg['data']}\n\n"

    async def broadcast(self, event: str, data: Any) -> None:
        await self.send(event, data)


_transport = SSETransport()


def shared_transport() -> SSETransport:
    """One registry: `tools/call` publishes from the JSON-RPC server and `/mcp/events` reads here.

    A per-module instance would have made the two sides of the stream invisible to each other.
    """
    return _transport

    """The endpoint for a path, or a failure naming it: a `for route in routes` loop that finds nothing

#### Thinking

Two failures, both real behaviours of my code:

1. `test_send_after_stop_delivers_nothing`: `stop()` pushes a `close` sentinel INTO the queue before clearing. So `q.empty()` is False — the queue holds the close frame. My assertion was wrong about the mechanism. Fix the test to assert what matters: after stop, a later `send()` adds nothing beyond the close sentinel → `q.qsize() == 1` and that one item is the close event. Better assertion: `[msg["event"] for msg in list(q._queue)] == ["close"]`.

2. `test_unsubscribing_ends_a_stream_still_reading`: timed out. Why? The consumer task is `[chunk async for chunk in t.stream(cid)]`. It's suspended inside `asyncio.wait_for(q.get())`. When I `unsubscribe`, nothing wakes the pending `q.get()` — the generator only re-checks membership AFTER a message arrives or a ping times out (30 s). So an abandoned-but-still-reading stream does NOT end promptly. That's true of the HTTP route too: if the client disconnects, the route's finally handles it via GeneratorExit... which we saw doesn't always run promptly.

Do I need to fix this in the product? The practical question: after `stop()`, the close sentinel wakes the pending get → stream ends. That's the shutdown path and it works (test_close_stops_stream passes). For the unsubscribe-while-reading case, the only way to end a pending get is to put something in the queue. So make `unsubscribe()` push a close sentinel into the queue it removes → the pending read wakes and the loop exits (membership check also fails → return). That's a genuine improvement: it makes "the client left" a delivered fact instead of a 30-second zombie holding a task and a queue.

Careful ordering in unsubscribe: pop the queue, then put_nowait close (queue may be full → suppress QueueFull).

And `stop()` also clears subscribers — it pushes close to each before clearing, fine.

    def _ruleset_denial(self, input_data: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
        """Why the shipped ruleset refuses this call, or None when it does not.

        Only a ``deny`` effect is acted on: a file can tighten what the operator configured, never
        widen it, so an ``allow`` effect falls through to the layers below. An unreadable ruleset
        refuses too — a policy that cannot be read is not a policy that permits everything.
        """
        try:
            from raven.core.security.policy_engine import PolicyLoadError, policy_engine
        except ImportError as exc:
            logger.debug("policy_engine not available: {}", exc)
            return None

        try:
            effect, rule_name = policy_engine.evaluate("tools", input_data)
        except PolicyLoadError as exc:
            logger.error("Tool policy ruleset unreadable, refusing: {}", exc)
            return f"policy ruleset unreadable ({exc})"

        if effect == "deny":
            return f"denied by policy rule '{rule_name}'"
        return None

    def denial_reason(self, tool_name: str) -> str | None:
        """Which layer refuses this call, in the words an operator can act on. None means it may run.

        Callers used to say `TOOLS_DENY` for every refusal this method returns, which became wrong
        the moment the ruleset gained a voice: a tool named only in `policy/tools.json` was reported
        as if the `TOOLS_DENY` switch had named it.
        """
